questions.q: A 30-year-old male presents with a painless ulcer on the glans penis for 2 weeks. On examination, the ulcer has indurated edges and a clean base. Inguinal lymph nodes are enlarged, firm, and non-tender. The most appropriate investigation is:
questions.exp: The clinical picture is classic primary syphilis (chancre). Dark field microscopy of the serous exudate from the ulcer base identifies Treponema pallidum spirochetes, which cannot be cultured or seen on Gram stain.

questions.q: A 25-year-old HIV-positive patient presents with multiple soft, flesh-coloured papules on the face and trunk with central umbilication. The most likely diagnosis is:
questions.exp: Molluscum contagiosum caused by a poxvirus presents with pearly, umbilicated papules. In HIV patients it is often widespread and giant lesions may occur. Tzanck smear shows Henderson-Patterson (molluscum) bodies.

questions.q: A 35-year-old farmer presents with a crusted, honey-coloured plaque on the chin with satellite lesions. Gram stain of the crust shows Gram-positive cocci. Which organism is most likely responsible?
questions.exp: Bullous impetigo is caused primarily by Staphylococcus aureus (phage group II, types 71/55) producing exfoliative toxins. Non-bullous impetigo involves both S. aureus and S. pyogenes, but S. aureus now predominates.

questions.q: A 40-year-old immunocompromised patient presents with a 3 cm boggy, fluctuant, pustular plaque on the scalp with broken-off hairs. Cervical lymphadenopathy is present. The most likely diagnosis is:
questions.exp: Kerion celsi is a severe inflammatory form of tinea capitis characterised by a boggy, purulent, tumour-like mass caused by a hypersensitivity reaction to dermatophytes (usually Trichophyton verrucosum or T. mentagrophytes). It requires systemic antifungal therapy.

questions.q: A 20-year-old student presents with hypopigmented anaesthetic patches on the trunk. Slit-skin smear from the lesion edge is negative. Skin biopsy shows granulomas around dermal nerves with Langhans giant cells but no bacilli. The most appropriate treatment is:
questions.exp: This is paucibacillary (PB) leprosy (tuberculoid type). WHO PB-MDT consists of Rifampicin 600 mg monthly supervised + Dapsone 100 mg daily for 6 months. MB-MDT (3 drugs, 12 months) is for multibacillary disease.

questions.q: A 50-year-old woman presents with tense bullae on normal and erythematous skin over the trunk and limbs with intense pruritus. DIF shows linear IgG and C3 at the dermal-epidermal junction. ELISA shows antibodies against BP180 and BP230. The diagnosis is:
questions.exp: Bullous pemphigoid (BP) presents with tense subepidermal bullae, pruritus, and IgG antibodies against hemidesmosomal proteins BP180 (type XVII collagen) and BP230. DIF shows linear IgG/C3 at BMZ. Pemphigus vulgaris shows intraepidermal blisters and anti-desmoglein antibodies.

questions.q: A 45-year-old woman presents with butterfly rash, photosensitivity, oral ulcers, and joint pain. ANA is positive (1:320, homogeneous). Which antibody is most specific for systemic lupus erythematosus?
questions.exp: Anti-Sm (anti-Smith) antibodies are highly specific (~99%) for SLE though present in only ~25% of patients. Anti-dsDNA is also specific and correlates with disease activity. Anti-Ro is associated with neonatal lupus. Anti-histone is seen in drug-induced lupus.

questions.q: A 60-year-old man presents with a pearly nodule with rolled telangiectatic borders and central ulceration on the nose. He has a history of chronic sun exposure. The most likely diagnosis is:
questions.exp: Nodulo-ulcerative BCC (rodent ulcer) has a pearly rolled border with telangiectasia and central ulceration on sun-exposed areas. It is locally invasive but rarely metastasises. Treatment is wide local excision or Mohs micrographic surgery.

questions.q: A 28-year-old woman on carbamazepine develops widespread erythema with epidermal detachment >30% BSA and mucosal erosions 3 weeks after starting the drug. The diagnosis and appropriate immediate action is:
opts: TEN — withdraw carbamazepine immediately and admit to burns/ICU
SJS — continue drug and add antihistamines
DRESS — start high-dose systemic steroids and continue carbamazepine
Erythema multiforme major — no drug withdrawal needed
questions.exp: TEN (>30% BSA epidermal detachment) and SJS (<10%) are life-threatening mucocutaneous reactions. Immediate withdrawal of the causative drug is the most critical step. SCORTEN score guides prognosis. Management: specialised burns unit, supportive care, consider cyclosporin or etanercept.

questions.q: A 22-year-old woman presents with well-demarcated depigmented macules on the dorsum of hands and perioral region. Wood's lamp examination shows chalk-white fluorescence enhancing the lesion contrast. The diagnosis is:
questions.exp: Vitiligo macules show chalk-white (brilliant white) fluorescence under Wood's lamp, enhancing contrast against surrounding skin. Pityriasis alba shows off-white hypopigmentation without complete depigmentation. Naevus depigmentosus is present from birth and stable.

questions.q: A 35-year-old man presents with palpable purpura over both legs, arthralgia, abdominal pain, and haematuria. IgA levels are elevated. Skin biopsy shows leukocytoclastic vasculitis with IgA deposits on DIF. The diagnosis is:
questions.exp: IgA vasculitis (HSP) is characterised by the tetrad of palpable purpura, arthralgia/arthritis, abdominal pain, and renal involvement. IgA deposition in vessel walls on DIF is pathognomonic. It is the most common systemic vasculitis in children but can occur in adults.

questions.q: A 30-year-old male presents with well-demarcated erythematous plaques with silvery-white scales on the elbows and knees. Auspitz sign is positive. The pathological hallmark on histology is:
questions.exp: Munro microabscesses are collections of neutrophils in the stratum corneum and are pathognomonic of psoriasis. Kogoj's spongiform pustule (neutrophils in spinous layer) is also seen in pustular psoriasis. Pautrier microabscesses are characteristic of mycosis fungoides.

questions.q: A 5-year-old child presents with intensely itchy vesicles on erythematous skin, predominantly in the antecubital and popliteal fossae. Serum IgE is markedly elevated. Family history reveals asthma in the mother. The most likely diagnosis is:
questions.exp: Atopic dermatitis presents in childhood with flexural involvement, intense pruritus, dry skin, and elevated IgE. It is part of the atopic triad (eczema, asthma, allergic rhinitis). Hanifin and Rajka criteria are used for diagnosis.

questions.q: During punch biopsy, the minimum recommended punch size for adequate histological diagnosis is:
questions.exp: A 4 mm punch biopsy is the standard minimum providing sufficient tissue for processing and diagnosis including epidermis, dermis, and subcutaneous fat. Smaller punches (2-3 mm) may be used for cosmetically sensitive areas but provide less tissue.

questions.q: A 32-year-old woman presents with grouped vesicles on an erythematous base in a dermatomal distribution on the right thorax, preceded by burning pain for 3 days. The causative virus establishes latency in:
questions.exp: Varicella-zoster virus (VZV) establishes latency in the dorsal root ganglia (and cranial nerve ganglia) after primary varicella infection. Reactivation causes herpes zoster, presenting with dermatomal vesicular eruption with prodromal pain.

questions.q: A 40-year-old diabetic man presents with painful, rapidly progressive necrotic ulcers on the legs with undermined violaceous edges and surrounding erythema. The diagnosis is:
questions.exp: Pyoderma gangrenosum (PG) is characterised by rapidly progressive painful ulcers with undermined violaceous boggy edges. It is associated with IBD, rheumatoid arthritis, and haematological malignancies. The pathergy phenomenon is characteristic. Treatment: systemic steroids or ciclosporin.

questions.q: A 55-year-old woman with a 10-year history of limited systemic sclerosis presents with telangiectasias, calcinosis cutis, Raynaud's phenomenon, oesophageal dysmotility, and sclerodactyly (CREST). Which antibody is most characteristically associated?
questions.exp: Anti-centromere antibodies (ACA) are found in 70-80% of limited cutaneous SSc (CREST syndrome). Anti-Scl-70 is associated with diffuse cutaneous SSc and pulmonary fibrosis. Anti-RNA pol III is associated with renal crisis in diffuse SSc.

questions.q: A 16-year-old boy presents with comedones, inflammatory papules, and nodules on the face, back, and chest. Which organism plays the primary pathogenic role in acne vulgaris?
questions.exp: Cutibacterium acnes (formerly Propionibacterium acnes) is central to acne pathogenesis, colonising the follicle and triggering inflammation via TLR2 activation and cytokine release. The four key factors in acne are: seborrhoea, follicular hyperkeratosis, C. acnes, and inflammation.

questions.q: A 38-year-old woman on long-term hydroxychloroquine for SLE develops bilateral central scotomas and bull's eye maculopathy on fundoscopy. The most sensitive screening tool for early detection of this toxicity is:
questions.exp: SD-OCT is the most sensitive tool for early detection of hydroxychloroquine retinopathy, showing parafoveal thinning before visual symptoms. Annual screening is recommended after 5 years of use. Safe dose is ≤5 mg/kg/day based on ideal body weight.

questions.q: A 28-year-old man presents with maculopapular rash on the trunk, palms, and soles, generalised lymphadenopathy, and mucous patches in the mouth 6 weeks after unprotected intercourse. RPR is reactive at 1:32. The treatment of choice is:
opts: Benzathine penicillin G 2.4 MU IM single dose
questions.exp: Secondary syphilis is treated with Benzathine penicillin G 2.4 MU IM as a single dose. Doxycycline 100 mg BD for 14 days is used in penicillin-allergic patients. Jarisch-Herxheimer reaction may occur 2-8 hours after treatment.

questions.q: A 45-year-old man presents with a well-demarcated, scaly, erythematous plaque on the trunk slowly enlarging for 2 years. Histology shows full-thickness epidermal dysplasia without dermal invasion. The diagnosis is:
questions.exp: Bowen's disease is squamous cell carcinoma in situ (full-thickness epidermal dysplasia without dermal invasion). Actinic keratosis shows only partial-thickness dysplasia. Treatment options include 5-FU, PDT, imiquimod, or excision.

questions.q: Which dermatophyte characteristically produces large, thin-walled, smooth, fusiform macroconidia and does NOT infect hair?
questions.exp: Epidermophyton floccosum produces characteristic club/beaver-tail shaped macroconidia in clusters, infects skin and nails but NOT hair. Microsporum canis produces large, spindle-shaped, thick-walled rough macroconidia. T. rubrum produces cigar-shaped macroconidia.

questions.q: A 70-year-old woman presents with intensely pruritic grouped vesicles on erythematous urticarial plaques, symmetrically on extensor surfaces. DIF of perilesional skin shows granular IgA deposits at the tips of dermal papillae. The diagnosis is:
questions.exp: Dermatitis herpetiformis (DH) is characterised by intensely pruritic grouped vesicles, granular IgA at dermal papillary tips on DIF, and association with gluten-sensitive enteropathy/coeliac disease. Treatment: gluten-free diet and dapsone. Linear IgA disease shows linear IgA at BMZ.

questions.q: A leprosy patient on MDT develops sudden erythema and swelling of pre-existing skin lesions, fever, and new nerve tenderness. There is NO new lesion formation and no systemic features. This reaction type is:
questions.exp: Type 1 (reversal) reaction occurs in borderline leprosy (BT, BB, BL) due to delayed hypersensitivity. Features: upgrading of existing skin lesions, new nerve palsies, NO new lesions, typically no systemic features. Treatment: prednisolone 40-60 mg/day tapered over 6 months.

questions.q: A 25-year-old man presents with soft, flesh-coloured cauliflower-like growths on the perianal region. The most common causative HPV types are:
questions.exp: Condyloma acuminata (anogenital warts) are caused by low-risk HPV types 6 and 11 in >90% of cases. HPV 16 and 18 are high-risk oncogenic types causing cervical and anal carcinomas. Treatment: podophyllotoxin, imiquimod, trichloroacetic acid, or surgical ablation.

questions.q: A 55-year-old chronic alcoholic presents with blistering on sun-exposed skin, hypertrichosis on the temples, milia, and hyperpigmentation. Urine shows pink-red fluorescence under Wood's lamp. The deficient enzyme is:
questions.exp: Porphyria cutanea tarda (PCT) results from reduced hepatic uroporphyrinogen decarboxylase activity. This leads to uroporphyrin accumulation causing photosensitivity, mechanobullous lesions, hypertrichosis, and pink-red urine fluorescence. Treatment: phlebotomy or low-dose hydroxychloroquine.

questions.q: A newborn presents with widespread blistering at birth. Electron microscopy shows cleavage within the lamina lucida of the basement membrane zone. The most likely diagnosis is:
questions.exp: In junctional EB (JEB), cleavage occurs within the lamina lucida of the BMZ involving proteins like laminin-332 or collagen XVII. EBS cleavage is intraepidermal (above BMZ); DEB is sub-lamina densa (below BMZ) involving type VII collagen.

questions.q: A 48-year-old woman on long-term minocycline for rosacea develops blue-grey pigmentation on the face and shins. The mechanism of minocycline-induced pigmentation is:
opts: Drug chelation with iron forming insoluble complexes deposited in dermis
Increased melanin synthesis stimulated by minocycline
questions.exp: Minocycline-induced pigmentation involves drug chelation with iron/calcium forming insoluble pigmented complexes deposited in dermal macrophages. Type I: blue-black in acne scars (iron-drug complex); Type II: blue-grey on shins/legs (melanin-drug complex); Type III: diffuse muddy-brown (melanin complex in sun-exposed skin).

questions.q: A 33-year-old woman presents with multiple firm, skin-coloured nodules on the scalp. Histology shows a cystic structure lined by stratified squamous epithelium WITHOUT a granular cell layer, filled with compact trichilemmal-type keratin. The diagnosis is:
questions.exp: Trichilemmal (pilar) cysts occur predominantly on the scalp, are lined by squamous epithelium WITHOUT a granular cell layer (abrupt keratinisation), and filled with homogeneous compact keratin. Epidermoid cysts have a granular cell layer and loose lamellar keratin.

questions.q: A 19-year-old woman presents with hypopigmented, finely scaling macules on the upper trunk that coalesce. KOH mount shows short hyphae and clusters of round yeast cells ('spaghetti and meatballs'). Which Wood's lamp colour is characteristic?
questions.exp: Pityriasis versicolor caused by Malassezia furfur shows yellow-green fluorescence under Wood's lamp. Coral pink is seen in erythrasma (Corynebacterium minutissimum producing porphyrins). Chalk-white fluorescence is seen in vitiligo. Microsporum tinea capitis shows blue-green fluorescence.

questions.q: A 62-year-old man presents with a slow-growing, violaceous, firm plaque on the lower leg that has been present for 20 years. Histology shows spindle cells forming slit-like vascular spaces with extravasated red blood cells and haemosiderin deposits. The diagnosis is:
questions.exp: Classic Kaposi's sarcoma occurs in elderly Mediterranean/Eastern European men and presents as violaceous plaques on lower extremities. Histology shows spindle cells with slit-like vascular spaces. HHV-8 is the causative agent. Unlike AIDS-related KS, classic type is indolent.
